body:
I am to assume it actually works like this
```suggestion
				Adds the cells inside the bounding box created from the [param begin] and [param end] points to the current selection.
				If [param active] is [code]false[/code], the cells inside the box are subtracted from the selection, instead.
```
Or, perhaps easier to digest:
```suggestion
				Adds the cells inside the given bounds to the current selection. The bounds are defined by the [param begin] and [param end] points.
				If [param active] is [code]false[/code], the cells inside the box are subtracted from the selection, instead.
```
Or similar.

I also personally think `active` should be moved to the end as an optional argument and given a more descriptive name.

body:
The selection changes to the box defined by the begin and end, it doesn't add anything. "Add" would imply that you can have multiple areas selected, but this isn't currently supported (it is something to be added later, so i also try to keep backwards compatibility in mind with what is exposed).

Perhaps something like "change the selection to a box from begin to end"?

Active doesn't mean add/subtract (the grid map editor currently only supports a box as a selection) but that there is a selection that can be used. I also think `active` isn't a good name (and i'd rather have something like `clear_selection` as a separate method) but it is what the rest of the code uses (actually the entire method just forwards the call to another with the exact same name and parameters, so i decided to leave it as is).
